title: fix: keep the openclaw command and Gateway working after updating a pnpm install
body:
## What Problem This Solves

When OpenClaw was installed with pnpm (`pnpm add -g openclaw`), a plain `openclaw update` could leave the machine with no `openclaw` command and no Gateway. This was measured in real Docker cells updating published 2026.11.4 to published 2026.11.5 with pnpm 11.28.13, 12.15.0 and 12.21.0:

- The live launcher pointed into the update's temporary stage directory, which no longer existed, so every `openclaw` command failed with `Cannot find module .../.openclaw-update-native-XXXXXX/.../openclaw.mjs`. On 12.15.0 the update even reported success.
- On pnpm 11.28.13 and 12.21.0 the Gateway restart was then refused with `managed-service-ownership (service-ownership-changed)`. The Gateway stayed down after the databases had been migrated (`state-migrated-no-rollback`).

## User Impact

User impact: pnpm-managed installs update to a working CLI and a Gateway serving the new version. If the published launcher still cannot start the new package after repair, the update fails and the transaction restores the previous launchers instead of reporting success.

Installs already updated by an older updater are repaired by the new package itself. Its Doctor (which runs during the update and on `openclaw doctor`) and its Gateway startup rewrite a launcher that provably belongs to this installation and still names a removed update stage, without a user command.

Update behavior for published updaters: the installed updater runs the launcher relocation, so 2026.11.4 and 2026.11.5 still publish a launcher that points into their stage when they update to a release with this fix. In the measured first hops (2026.11.4 and 2026.11.5, each to this fix, pnpm 12.21.0), the new package's Doctor repaired that launcher during the same update. Both updaters handed the post-core steps to the new package (`update-driver-handoff`), which restarted the Gateway on the new version. Both runs ended with exit 0, a working CLI and the Gateway serving the new version. The service-ownership refusal fired only when the new package lacked the fix (2026.11.4 to public 2026.11.5).

## Why This Change Was Made

Launcher (A): pnpm writes shims as `exec node  "$basedir_abs"/'../global/v11/<group>/node_modules/openclaw/openclaw.mjs' "$@"`, with the base and the target quoted separately. The relocation pattern only recognized `"$basedir_abs/<target>"`, so the stage-relative target was published unchanged. #170131 fixed the unquoted `$basedir_abs/` form; the quoted form was never handled. This change:
- teaches relocation and verification the quoted form;
- refuses to finalize, before the Gateway is stopped, a staged launcher that relocation still leaves pointing into the stage;
- makes the post-activation check resolve every launcher target. A launcher whose target is missing is repaired, or the update fails. An unreadable format keeps the existing warning.

Service (B): before stopping the Gateway, the updater records the service as owned by the lexical pnpm global entry (`global/v11/<group>/node_modules/openclaw`). The unit runs the real path that entry resolved to in pnpm's versioned store (`store/v11/links/@/openclaw/<old>/...`). The swap repoints the entry to the new version. Revalidation's install-root-change check then re-inspected the unchanged unit against that same lexical root, which now means the new version, and found it "foreign". This only happens while the old store directory still exists; when pnpm has pruned it, the existing "unresolved" path already passed. Revalidation now also matches the unchanged definition against its own installation root. The protection is unchanged: the definition fingerprint, service name, profile and manager UID must still be the ones admitted before the stop, so an edited definition, or a service of another installation, is still refused.

## Evidence

Behavior checked: an ordinary pnpm package update keeps a working CLI and restarts the Gateway on the new version, and an already-broken launcher heals.

- RED (published updaters): 2026.11.4 to public 2026.11.5 on pnpm 12.21.0 (image default), managed Gateway. Exit 1, CLI broken with `Cannot find module '<pnpm-home>/.openclaw-update-native-6MD67E/v11/926ea…/node_modules/openclaw/openclaw.mjs'`, Gateway down. The same result was measured on 11.28.13; on 12.15.0 the update reported ok and the CLI was broken.
- GREEN-2 (updater from this head): an installed build of `1f1a842` (relabeled 2026.11.19-beta.1) updated through pnpm 12.21.0 to a newer build of the same code labeled beta.2 (`openclaw update --yes --json --tag <tarball>`). Exit 0, status ok. `openclaw --version` prints `OpenClaw 2026.11.19-beta.2 (1f1a842)`. The live launcher runs `"${basedir_abs}"/../global/v11/926ea…/node_modules/openclaw/openclaw.mjs`, and neither it nor NODE_PATH names a stage. The Gateway serves beta.2 with `/readyz` 200, and the service definition was refreshed to the new root. A second update returned `already-current` with the CLI and Gateway still working. The final head `298d125` only adds a merge of two main commits that touch release-validation tooling and docs, so the cell was not rerun for it. The same cell also passed on `387a694`.
- First hop (published 2026.11.5 updater to this head): published `2026.11.5` installed with `pnpm add -g` on pnpm 12.21.0, updated to a build of the PR head `387a694` with `openclaw update --yes --json --tag <tarball>`. Exit 0, status ok. Afterwards `openclaw --version` prints `OpenClaw 2026.11.19-beta.2` and the Gateway serves it with `/readyz` 200. A file observer shows the published updater still writing the broken launcher (`exec node  "$basedir_abs"/'../.openclaw-update-native-WeztE4/v11/…/openclaw.mjs'`; its own check only warned, "Published launcher … could not be verified"). Twelve seconds later, during the post-swap Doctor that runs from this head's package, the launcher was rewritten to `../global/v11/926ea…/node_modules/openclaw/openclaw.mjs`. The Gateway restart did not hit the ownership refusal on this hop, because 2026.11.5 hands the post-core steps to the candidate driver (`update-driver-handoff`), which contains the revalidation fix. A second update returned `already-current`. The same first hop from published `2026.11.4` (on the earlier head `70e18af`) also ended with exit 0, a working CLI and the Gateway serving the new version.
- Unit tests, red on main and green on this head:
  - `update-native-package-stage.test.ts`: a pnpm layout with the quoted shim, under a directory named `team's base` and with NODE_PATH in the stage. On main the published launcher runs `Module not found ".../physical/bin/../.openclaw-update-native-…/openclaw.mjs"`. A second case refuses to finalize an `openclaw` launcher that relocation cannot rewrite and leaves another package's shim alone.
  - `update-runtime-relocation.test.ts`: with a symlinked bin directory, a lexical shim resolves beside the link and a shim that assigns `basedir_abs` resolves physically.
  - `update-command-service-install-root.test.ts`: a pnpm versioned-store layout with the old store kept. On main this fails with the exact production error (`Required: admitted service ownership owned … detected: foreign`). The pruned-store case and two negative controls (another installation, an edited definition) are green on both.
  - `package-update-swap.launchers.test.ts`: the earlier "commit with a warning" contract for missing launcher targets is replaced by a failed swap that keeps the previous package; an unknown launcher format still commits with the actionable warning.
  - `update-launcher-repair.test.ts`: the exact shim text from the RED evidence is repaired and executes the live install, including under a global directory named `team's global` (the `'\''` quoting round-trips and the shim still runs). The same cases run with an apostrophe above the pnpm home and with a directory named `odd "dir" $HOME \ global`; a stub `node` checks the exact entry and NODE_PATH. A FIFO named `openclaw` on PATH is skipped. The mode is preserved, no staging is left behind, and a second pass leaves the launcher alone. Four cases are left untouched: a live stage (update in progress), another installation's root, a recorded entry that is not the stage's live counterpart, and a stage that is not beside the project. The "another installation" and "stage not beside the project" cases were shown to fail with their guard removed.
  - `server-startup-plugins.test.ts`: Gateway post-ready maintenance repairs a home-level launcher on PATH that names this installation and a removed stage, and logs the repair.
- Recovery for an already-bricked 2026.11.4/2026.11.5 install, run in the cell: `pnpm add -g --allow-build=openclaw openclaw@2026.11.5`, `openclaw gateway install --force`, `openclaw gateway restart`, then `openclaw gateway status --deep` and `openclaw doctor --non-interactive`, all exit 0. The CLI and Gateway work afterwards. `openclaw update status` still lists the failed run and an unresolved original-state capture; keep it and the `<PNPM_HOME>/.openclaw.package-backup-*` directory until Doctor passes.

<details><summary>Checks</summary>

- On the final head: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` on the touched and adjacent files (launcher repair, runtime relocation, native stage, all `package-update-swap*`, runtime path index, service install root, update rollback, Doctor startup, Gateway startup plugins) all pass except `update-command-rollback.test.ts > excludes a competing config writer…`. That test asserts a setgid mode bit (`expected 504 to be 1528`) and fails the same way on main on macOS, a known Mac-only failure. Earlier heads also ran the 75 affected files with the same single exception.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`: pass. `oxlint` on touched files: clean. Test-lines ratchet: +424 against 400 plus the recorded 24. `pnpm check:import-cycles` and `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles`: 0 cycles.
- The commits cherry-pick cleanly onto `release/2026.11.6` (#201739) and `release/2026.11.10` (#201740).
- `autoreview` does not run on this machine.
</details>

### Recordings

Raw terminal recordings of the Docker cells. Each shows the cell log streamed live, then a summary read from the raw cell files. Host paths are replaced with `<proof-dir>`; container paths are under `/home/appuser`.

- RED, then recovery: published 2026.11.4 to public 2026.11.5 on pnpm 12.21.0, followed by the recovery commands.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/14ca724c-7d38-418e-b67c-8c3777ec4330

- GREEN-2: head `1f1a842` to head `1f1a842`.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/af1fcdb0-aebb-47f5-93d7-ff4554c3dd3b

- GREEN-1 (first hop): published 2026.11.5 to head `387a694`.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/95ddf49a-93fc-41bd-8e1b-f24cf83de427

Full raw cell logs are not attached, because the Crabbox artifact store rejects uploads from this machine. The decisive lines are quoted above.

### Review rounds

Landing review on `387a694` found that the launcher rewrite missed pnpm's escaped spelling when the stage path itself contains an apostrophe. With a pnpm home under `team's base/`, pnpm writes the stage in `NODE_PATH` as `team'\''s base/...`, and the raw prefix replacement never matched it. The repair then left NODE_PATH on the removed stage but still reported success, and the pre-stop guard would have refused every update on such an install. It also found that the pattern stopped at a `"` inside a single-quoted target. Both were real and are fixed in `3df4ba4`. Relocation now parses each shell word, rewrites its value and quotes it again, so every quoting form is handled the same way. Coverage, all red on `387a694` and green now:
- the repair, with the apostrophe below and above the pnpm home and with a directory named `odd "dir" $HOME \ global`;
- the updater (finalize), with an apostrophe in the stage path. A stub `node` checks the exact entry path and NODE_PATH the shell passes.

"Repaired" is reported only when nothing in the launcher still names the stage. The two refusal cases that previously never found a launcher now present one, and each fails when its guard is removed. The private repair directory is removed when the first write fails. Docs now say exactly what the first-hop runs showed.

ClawSweeper round 2 on `3df4ba4` rated it overall D / proof C / patch D. All five findings were real and are fixed in `8db0790`:
- Base directory choice used a textual `$basedir_abs` match, which missed the braced `${basedir_abs}` the rewriter emits. A shim whose bin directory is a symlink would then resolve its target from the wrong parent. Relocation and verification now use the physical bin directory whenever the shim defines `basedir_abs`.
- On Windows, absolute paths in extensionless shell shims lost the forward-slash spelling pass. Shell words and comments now get the same native and forward-slash passes as `.cmd`/`.ps1` shims.
- The repair scan read every PATH candidate before checking its type, so a FIFO named `openclaw` blocked Doctor and Gateway maintenance. It now skips anything that is not a regular file. A new test with a FIFO on PATH times out without the check and passes with it.
- Post-activation verification parsed each launcher twice. `verifyRuntimeLauncher` now returns `unknown-format` from its single read; the swap turns that into the warning and still fails a missing target.
- Docs: automatic launcher repair is macOS and Linux only; Windows users follow the reinstall steps.

ClawSweeper round 3 on `3fdf10a` (round 2's fixes merged with main) rated it overall D / proof C / patch D. All four findings were real and are fixed in `98bad55`:
- The pre-stop guard inspected every file in the staged bin directory, so another global package's shim that still named the stage failed the OpenClaw update. It now checks only the launchers the swap publishes (`resolvePackageUpdateLauncherNames`). A new negative control (`other-cli`) finalizes; the `openclaw` case still refuses. The control fails when the filter is removed.
- Physical-base detection matched any text containing `basedir_abs`, including a directory name in a path. It now requires the shim to assign `basedir_abs`. The new verification test with a lexical shim, a symlinked bin directory and a path that names `basedir_abs` fails on the textual check.
- The repair checked ownership on one read and relocated a second read. Ownership (`cmd-shim-target` equals this installation's entry) is now checked inside the repair, on the same bytes it relocates. If the launcher changed before the rename, the repair leaves it alone. That race is not covered by a test.
- The recovery command lacked `--allow-build=openclaw`. The docs, Doctor and Gateway messages now use `pnpm add -g --allow-build=openclaw openclaw@<installed-version>`, the command the recovery cell ran.

Shrinking the Gateway startup test to a home-level layout (`PNPM_HOME/openclaw` beside `PNPM_HOME/global/`) exposed one more gap, fixed in `1f1a842`. In that layout the stage sits inside the launcher's own directory, and an in-place repair kept the target unchanged, treating it as moving with the directory. A launcher rewritten in place now applies the stage relocation. The updater relocates between different directories and is unchanged. The Gateway test fails without this fix.

The same commit consolidates tests:
- the apostrophe-in-stage finalize case is folded into the quoted pnpm 12 layout;
- the FIFO case is folded into the four rewrite cases;
- the verification cases and the service revalidation cases each become one table;
- "recorded target missing" is dropped, because the ownership check now covers it the same way as "another installation".

After that, 24 regression-test lines remain over the 400-line allowance (21 before the landing round). They are recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/201735-pnpm-update-keeps-cli-and-gateway.txt`.


ClawSweeper round 1 on `df6345e` rated it overall F / proof C / patch F. Its findings and the independent reviewer's were all checked and fixed in `bc6c5e9`:
- Pnpm paths containing `'` broke the rewritten single-quoted shim: real. Relocation now decodes and re-encodes `'\''` both in the exec target and in the NODE_PATH export, and a repaired shim under `team's global` runs.
- First-hop repair only looked in PNPM_HOME: real for a bin directory configured elsewhere. It now also scans PATH entries, and still writes only a launcher whose `cmd-shim-target` is this installation's entry.
- The repair wrote through a predictable temporary name: real. It now writes the analyzed content into a private `mkdtemp` directory beside the launcher and renames from there.
- Doctor swallowed repair failures: real. Doctor and the Gateway now report each launcher they could not repair, with the reinstall command.
- The service fixture was systemd-only: real. Those cases are skipped on Windows, with the reason stated.
- From the independent reviewer: the repair branch inside the post-activation check was unreachable (the pre-stop guard already refuses), so it was removed. Docs updated. Assertions added for the launcher half of a failed swap and for the untouched project after a pre-stop refusal.

### Landing round on `298d125`

The required `check-guards-architecture` job failed on a new import cycle: `update-native-package-stage.ts` → `package-update-filesystem.ts` → `package-update-swap-contract.ts` → back. `resolvePackageUpdateLauncherNames` now lives in a leaf module, `package-update-launcher-names.ts`, and all four callers import it from there. `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles` reported 1 cycle before and 0 after; `pnpm check:import-cycles` passes. The new module is listed in the update-restart swap fixture and in the PR wrapper inventory, and their tests pass.

Two smaller fixes from the same round:
- Absolute-path relocation used `replaceAll` with a string replacement, so a `$'` in the live path was read as a replacement token. A callback replaces it now. The repair quoting case now uses a directory named `odd "dir" $HOME $' \ global`; it fails with the string replacement and passes with the callback.
- The pre-stop refusal now names the direct pnpm reinstall, `openclaw gateway install --force` and `openclaw gateway restart`, which is the sequence the recovery cell ran, plus `openclaw triage`. The finalize test asserts the full message.

No new rating round or Docker cell was run for these. The launcher writer is unchanged except in the `$'` case, which has the unit test.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- A lexical `basedir` shim reached through a symlinked bin directory is relocated from the physical directory. The repair then correctly reports it as not repaired (`update-launcher-repair.ts`, the relocation step) instead of repairing it.
- The repair writes, rereads and rewrites its temporary file. This costs only efficiency.
- Two not-ours tests find no launcher at all and need `PNPM_HOME` set to exercise a real one.
- An empty private repair directory can be left behind if the first write fails.

## Steps left to a person

- An install already bricked by a published updater whose Gateway is down needs the recovery commands above, or `openclaw triage`, because no new code is running there yet. Once this release is installed (for example by the recovery's `pnpm add`), its Doctor and Gateway repair the launcher themselves.

## Not proven

- The Windows `.cmd`/`.ps1` quoted forms were not observed; those formats keep the existing behavior.
- Bun global installs are unchanged and were not run end to end.
- Which pnpm binary the updater invokes: `resolvePnpmCommand` prefers `PNPM_HOME/bin/pnpm` over PATH. In these cells no pnpm was installed in `PNPM_HOME`, so the image's pnpm ran. Every pnpm tried (11.28.13, 12.15.0, 12.21.0) wrote or rewrote the quoted form, so the fix does not depend on the version.
